body_text: View All News Sammy Hagar Brings His Hit Best of All Worlds Tour to Colorado Springs July 17, 2026 Just Off a Sold-Out UK Tour, Rock Icon Returns to VENU's Ford Amphitheater August 13 Tickets On Sale Friday, July 24 at 10 a.m. MT Photos available HERE COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Venu Holding Corporation ("VENU" or the "Company") (NYSE AMERICAN: VENU) announced today that on the heels of his sold-out UK tour, Rock & Roll Hall of Famer Sammy Hagar brings his acclaimed Best of All Worlds Tour to the Company’s Ford Amphitheater in Colorado Springs on Thursday, August 13 . Sammy Hagar Brings His Hit Best of All Worlds Tour to Colorado Springs - Thursday, August 13 Hagar is joined by the Best of All Worlds Band featuring fellow Rock & Roll Hall of Famer Michael Anthony , guitar virtuoso Joe Satriani , powerhouse drummer Kenny Aronoff , and keyboardist Spider Cherry . Together, they perform a career-spanning set celebrating more than five decades of rock history, including favorites from Montrose, Sammy's solo career, Chickenfoot and Van Halen. "We've been having a blast on this tour, and every night this band just keeps getting better," said Sammy Hagar. "Colorado Springs has been a long time coming and we're ready to rock the Rockies!" "The last time I saw Sammy play, I was a sophomore in high school, sneaking in over the fence just to catch the show. Now, to host him right here in Colorado Springs, that's something I'll never take for granted," said J.W. Roth, Founder, Chairman, and CEO of VENU. Colorado has played host to some of the biggest moments of Sammy Hagar's live career—from Van Halen's 5150 Tour stadium show at Folsom Field in Boulder in 1986 and the legendary Monsters of Rock festival at Denver's Mile High Stadium in 1988 to a sold-out Best of All Worlds Tour performance at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in 2024. Now, fresh off a sold-out UK tour, Hagar brings his hit Best of All Worlds Tour to Ford Amphitheater in Colorado Springs on August 13. Artist presales begin Monday, July 20 at 10 a.m. MT , with additional venue, promoter and radio presales beginning Wednesday, July 22. Tickets go on sale to the general public on Friday, July 24 at 10 a.m. MT . Tickets are available via AXS Tickets HERE and visit RedRocker.com for complete information and ticket links. ABOUT SAMMY HAGAR For more than five decades, Sammy Hagar has been recognized as one of the best and most accomplished lead singers and songwriters in rock music. From breaking into the industry with the seminal hard rock band Montrose, to his multi-platinum solo career, to his ride as the frontman of Van Halen, Chickenfoot, The Circle, and more, Hagar has amassed 25 Platinum albums on sales surpassing 50 million worldwide. Along his journey, he has set the tone for some of the greatest rock anthems ever written with songs like "I Can't Drive 55," "Right Now," and "Why Can't This Be Love," and earned the highest respect of the music industry with a Grammy Award and induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Since opening his flagship Cabo Wabo Cantina in 1990, he’s turned a lifelong passion for great food, music and spirits into a thriving and iconic lifestyle brand encompassing restaurants and spirits. A pioneer in the spirits industry, he launched Cabo Wabo Tequila in 1996 and catapulted it into the #2-selling premium tequila brand in the United States. In 2010, Hagar sold his interests in Cabo Wabo Tequila to Gruppo Campari in a 9-figure deal that’s widely credited as the start of the celebrity-owned spirits trend. He now owns an award-winning portfolio of top-shelf spirits and beer that embody that same spirit of Baja beach life and rock ‘n’ roll. They include Sammy’s Beach Bar Rum, a partnership with rock icon Rick Springfield, Santo Spirits, a partnership with tastemaker Guy Fieri, and Red Rocker Brewing Co. Never one to hit the brakes, Sammy’s also expanded his successes into publishing, TV, radio and beyond, including five seasons of his hit TV show “Rock & Roll Road Trip with Sammy Hagar” and as host of “Sammy Hagar’s Top Rock Countdown,” a weekly syndicated radio show on 90+ US stations. He’s a #1 NYT bestselling author, a dedicated philanthropist—donating millions back to local communities through his private non-profit The Hagar Family Foundation , and the first Honorary Ambassador to Los Cabos, an honor he was bestowed in 2022 in recognition of his longtime investment in the people and economy of Mexico. Visit RedRocker.com for more information. About Venu Holding Corporation Venu Holding Corporation ("VENU") (NYSE American: VENU) is a premier owner, developer, and operator of luxury, experience-driven entertainment destinations. Founded by Colorado Springs entrepreneur J.W. Roth, VENU has a portfolio of premium brands that includes Ford Amphitheater, Sunset Amphitheaters, Phil Long Music Hall, The Hall at Bourbon Brothers, Bourbon Brothers Smokehouse and Tavern, Aikman Owners Clubs, and Roth’s Sea & Steak. With venues operating and in development across Colorado, Georgia, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas and a nationwide expansion underway, VENU is setting a new standard for live entertainment. VENU has been recognized nationally by The Wall Street Journal , The New York Times , Billboard , VenuesNow , and Variety for its innovative and disruptive approach to live entertainment. Through strategic partnerships with industry leaders such as AEG Presents, NFL Hall of Famer and Founder of EIGHT Elite Light Beer, Troy Aikman, Billboard, Aramark Sports + Entertainment, Tixr, Boston Common Golf, Niall Horan, and Dierks Bentley, VENU continues to shape the future of the entertainment landscape. For more information, visit VENU’s website , Instagram , LinkedIn , or X . Improving Hotel Operational Efficiency for Revenue Growth: Key Strategies to Success
summary: A guide for hoteliers on how to improve hotel operational efficiency. Learn strategies and tech solutions to reduce costs and drive significant revenue growth.
body_text: Running a profitable hotel has never been more complex. Every missed call, slow check-in and inefficient task eats into both margins and revenue opportunities. Labor costs continue to rise and guest expectations keep climbing, while 76% of hotels have faced staffing difficulties, according to recent industry survey data from the American Hotel & Lodging Association (AHLA) . That’s why hotel operational efficiency matters more than ever. Smarter operations cut costs, free up staff time, improve the guest experience and make you more money in the process. In this guide, we’ll break down practical operational strategies that help you save and make money. Key Takeaways Operational efficiency drives both cost savings and revenue growth: The right technology eliminates repetitive tasks while helping you upsell and improve guest satisfaction. AI and automation are becoming core parts of modern hotel operations: Hotels are rapidly investing in AI-powered workflows to improve communications, reduce workload and increase efficiency. Hospitality-specific platforms like Canary give hotels a competitive edge: Unified guest engagement systems connect operations, guest communications and revenue opportunities into one experience. What is Hotel Operational Efficiency? Hotel operational efficiency is optimizing resources (e.g. staff time, energy usage and supplies) while streamlining workflows to reduce waste, lower costs and improve overall guest satisfaction . It’s less about cutting costs, and more about using smarter processes and technology to simplify operations across departments like front desk, housekeeping and guest services. When your hotel is operationally efficient, it looks like: Faster guest service Reduced labor strain Better staff productivity Increased ancillary revenue Higher guest satisfaction scores The Core Functions of Hotel Operations Management Before improving operational efficiency, it’s important to understand the core departments that keep a hotel running day to day. Hotel operations typically center around four key functions: Front Office Housekeeping Food & Beverage Sales & Marketing Each department plays a direct role in shaping both operational performance and the guest experience. When these teams operate efficiently and stay connected, hotels reduce friction, improve service and unlock stronger revenue opportunities. For the specific roles and responsibilities of each department, read our comprehensive guide on Hotel Operations and Management . How Streamlined Operations Make You More Money Think of hotel operational efficiency as the trunk of a tree, feeding the branches of revenue and guest satisfaction . When operations need less attention, staff spend more time delivering personalized guest experiences. Faster service, better communication and fewer operational bottlenecks are all key strategies for increasing revenue, because they all contribute to stronger hotel operations. Improved guest service leads to better reviews and repeat bookings. Higher operational efficiency reduces overhead and offers more room for upsell fulfillment. It’s a win-win-win all around. Automate Hotel Operations: Reduced Labor Costs = Higher Profit Margins Mundane tasks, like answering common guest questions, managing check-ins, sending guest communications and processing routine requests can all be improved through automation. AI-powered solutions work in the background to complete these repetitive tasks, so staff can focus on more high-impact interactions. This improves the consistency of your hotel’s service, but it also serves to directly benefit staff. Instead of ending the day with the mental fatigue that quickly begets burnout, staff get to create meaningful connections with every guest. Faster, Smoother Service = Better Reviews & More Repeat Business Efficient hotel operations create a better guest experience at every interaction. It’s easier to build guest satisfaction when guests receive quick responses, easy check-ins and personalized service without delays or friction. That smoother experience has a direct impact on loyalty and revenue. Happy guests are more likely to leave positive reviews, return for future stays and recommend your property to others — all of which strengthen long-term profitability! More Staff Time for High-Value Tasks = Increased Upsell Revenue Juggling routine requests and manual processes is a drain on resources and on brain space. Instead, empower your teams to spend more time delivering personalized guest service , recommending upgrades and creating the memorable interactions that make a truly great stay. Automation also creates new opportunities to surface upsells throughout the guest journey, from room upgrades to late checkout and on-property add-ons. More ancillary revenue, more guest personalization and less work for staff means everyone stands to benefit. 5 Strategies to Improve Operational Efficiency in the Hospitality Industry Hotels often focus on cutting costs when they want to improve hotel operations. But the biggest gains come from improving workflows, reducing friction and giving staff more time to focus on guests. Strong hotel operations and management strategies create smoother experiences for both staff and travelers, while unlocking new revenue opportunities in the process Here are some helpful tips. 1. Automate the Arrival & Departure Workflow Manual check-ins and checkouts are some of the biggest bottlenecks to operational efficiency in the hotel industry. Front desk teams spend valuable time handling paperwork, processing payments and answering repetitive questions, all while guests wait in line after a long day of travel. Automating the arrival and departure experience is one of the fastest ways to reduce this friction. Solutions like Canary’s Mobile Check-In and Smart Checkout streamline the entire workflow by reducing lobby congestion and dramatically cutting staff workload. Hotels that automate arrivals and departures create a better first (and final) impression while automating offers for popular add-ons like early check-in or late checkout. 2. Unify Your Guest Communication Channels Fragmented guest communication creates operational chaos. When staff rely on phone calls, paper notes or other disconnected systems to manage requests, it’s inevitable that messages will get lost in the process. Centralized Guest Messaging solves this by bringing communication into one organized platform. Staff can manage guest conversations across channels while automating routine interactions to improve response times. This gives guests the instant, accurate service they expect, while reducing service misses and staff interruptions. 3. Digitize Your Contracting and Payment Authorizations Manual sales and payment workflows slow down operations and create unnecessary security risks. Printing, scanning, emailing and storing paper authorization forms wastes staff time while increasing the risk of fraud and processing errors. Digital Contracts and Digital Authorizations modernize these workflows by automating approvals, signatures and payment verification in one secure system. This reduces administrative work while boosting efficiency, and prevents any headaches from compliance issues down the road. 4. Implement AI to Handle Routine Inquiries Hotel teams spend a surprising amount of time answering the same questions every day: “What time is check-in? Do you offer parking? Is the pool open? Can I request a late checkout?” These repetitive interactions create constant interruptions for staff, slowing down service and increasing the likelihood of service errors. Canary’s AI Guest Messaging acts as a digital front desk agent, instantly answering common guest questions 24/7 and escalating more complex issues to staff. This improves response speed, and hotel staff actually have time to focus on the higher-value guest interactions. 5. Empower Guests with Self-Service Options Travelers increasingly prefer self-service options so they can get service on their terms. For front desk workers, self-service tools reduce operational strain by minimizing repetitive guest requests. That makes it a win for both guests and hotel teams. Solutions like Self-Service Kiosks and Digital Compendiums allow guests to check in and access hotel information without waiting for staff assistance. Whether the guest arrives after-hours or at a busy time, they’ll be able to get the instant service they expect. Efficiency is About Saving and Making Money The most successful hotels see operational efficiency as a growth strategy. Smoother hotel operations result in better staff efficiency and guest service. Plus, revenue opportunities become easier to capture at every stage of the guest journey. From automating check-in workflows to streamlining guest communication and implementing AI-powered service tools, efficient hotel operations create measurable business impact. Operational Strategy How it SAVES Money (Cost Reduction) How it MAKES Money (Revenue Growth) Automated Workflows Reduces labor costs by requiring fewer staff hours for administrative tasks like data entry and filing. Increases Revenue Per Available Room by allowing for faster turnover, meaning guests can get into their rooms quickly. Unified Communication Prevents costly service recovery (e.g., comping a meal or a night's stay) caused by missed requests or errors. Enables targeted, real-time offers (like late checkout or spa deals) directly to the guest's phone. Digital Payments Minimizes financial loss from manual errors, "friendly fraud" and chargebacks through secure, verified links. Speeds up the sales cycle for group bookings and events, allowing the sales team to close more deals in less time. AI Messaging Lowers overhead by handling high-volume interactions without increasing headcount. Improves the guest experience by providing instant answers and personalized offers 24/7. Self-Service Options Decreases the amount of time and space needed to manage simple guest needs and information sharing. Increases ancillary revenue by making it incredibly easy for guests to browse and book amenities, room service or tours. Ready to build a more efficient and profitable hotel? Discover how Canary’s platform streamlines operations to drive revenue. FAQs Why is operational efficiency important for hotels? Operational efficiency is important because it directly impacts both profitability and the guest experience. Efficient hotels reduce wasted time, streamline workflows and lower operational costs while delivering faster, more personalized service. This improves guest satisfaction, increases staff productivity and creates more opportunities for revenue growth through upsells, repeat bookings and stronger online reviews. What are examples of hotel operational efficiency? Examples of hotel operational efficiency include automating repetitive tasks, streamlining workflows, optimizing inventory management, implementing energy-saving measures, improving employee training and adopting advanced hospitality technology. How do you improve operational efficiency in hotels? Hotels improve operational efficiency by reducing manual work, automating repetitive processes and connecting systems across departments. The most effective strategies often include digitizing the guest journey, centralizing communication, implementing AI-powered tools and offering self-service options for guests. Strong hotel operations and management strategies focus on creating smoother workflows that improve both staff productivity and guest satisfaction at the same time. How does technology help improve efficiency in the hospitality industry? Technology improves hospitality efficiency by automating time-consuming tasks, reducing operational bottlenecks and giving staff faster access to information. Tools like Canary’s Mobile Check-In, Guest Messaging, AI Voice and Smart Checkout reduce manual workload while improving service speed and consistency. Connected hospitality platforms also improve communication between departments, helping hotels operate more smoothly while delivering better guest experiences. How quickly can hotels typically see ROI from operational improvements? The speed of ROI often depends on the size of the property, existing workflows and the specific technology being implemented, but operational efficiency improvements typically deliver both short-term savings and long-term revenue growth. Many hotels begin seeing ROI from operational improvements within a few weeks, especially when implementing automation and guest-facing technology. Faster check-ins, reduced labor strain, improved upsell conversion and fewer missed guest requests create immediate operational and revenue impact.

title: Mastering DomainKeys Identified Mail Gmail in 2026
summary: Boost deliverability! Learn DomainKeys Identified Mail Gmail setup, checks, & fixes. This 2026 guide helps improve your email deliverability.
body_text: A founder sends a campaign from Google Workspace, the copy is solid, the list is clean, and Gmail still pushes replies into spam or filters the message out. In many cases, the problem isn't the email itself. It's DKIM. DomainKeys Identified Mail for Gmail is the digital signature Gmail uses to decide whether a message really came from the domain it claims to come from, and whether that message was changed on the way. If DKIM is missing or failing, Gmail treats the message as less trustworthy, which directly hurts inbox placement. What Is DKIM and Why Is It Critical for Gmail A founder can send a legitimate email from Google Workspace and still lose the inbox if Gmail cannot verify who signed that message. That is the practical job of DKIM. DKIM , short for DomainKeys Identified Mail, adds a digital signature to outgoing mail. Gmail checks that signature against a public key stored in your DNS. If the signature matches, Gmail gets proof that the message was authorized by the signing domain and that key parts of the email were not changed after it left your system. Why Gmail pays close attention to DKIM Gmail uses authentication to decide how much trust to give a message before engagement data even enters the picture. A valid DKIM signature helps confirm that the email was sent by infrastructure tied to the domain in the header, and that the content stayed intact in transit. That matters because Gmail does not judge deliverability on copy alone. It evaluates identity, consistency, and reputation together. In practice, DKIM failures show up as business problems first. Reply rates drop. Outreach gets ignored. Password resets and onboarding emails arrive late or in spam. Teams often blame the sending tool or the subject line, but the underlying issue is that Gmail cannot verify the message cleanly. What DKIM actually proves, and what it does not DKIM proves two things: The message was signed by a server with access to the domain's private key. The signed parts of the message were not altered after sending. It does not prove the sender is reputable. It does not stop spam by itself. It does not replace SPF or DMARC. That distinction matters. A domain can have DKIM set up and still struggle with inbox placement if reputation is weak, the sending pattern is erratic, or DMARC alignment is broken. Why founders should care DKIM is often treated as a DNS setup task. The better way to view it is as an inbox trust control. If your company depends on email for revenue, hiring, support, product notifications, or customer onboarding, DKIM affects whether those messages are treated as legitimate before a human ever sees them. That is why I do not recommend stopping at "record published." Confirm whether Gmail is validating the signature on live mail. A quick DKIM checker for your domain can confirm the DNS side, but the definitive diagnosis comes from the Gmail headers, where you can see why a signature passed, failed, or was ignored. Where DKIM fits with SPF and DMARC Authentication layer What it checks Why it matters DKIM Whether the message was signed by the domain and stayed intact Helps Gmail verify message integrity SPF Whether the sending server is allowed to send for the domain Helps verify the sending source DMARC Whether DKIM or SPF aligns with the visible From domain, and what to do when checks fail Ties authentication to enforcement The short version is simple. If DKIM is missing, broken, or signing with the wrong domain, Gmail has less reason to trust the message. Most setup guides stop at adding the DNS record. The harder and more useful skill is reading Gmail's headers so you can connect a DKIM error to the actual problem, which is mail going to spam. How to Check DKIM Status in Gmail A founder sends a launch email, sees solid open rates in one segment and silence in another, then assumes the copy missed. The faster check is Gmail's header view. It shows whether Gmail trusted the message enough to treat it like legitimate mail or held it back because the DKIM signature did not verify. That is the part many setup guides skip. They show the DNS record. Gmail shows the verdict. Start with the clue Gmail shows first Open the message in Gmail and look near the sender details. If Gmail shows a via domain, treat it as a clue, not a conclusion. It often means the message passed through another platform, such as a CRM, help desk, or marketing tool, and that matters because the signing domain may not match the domain your recipient sees in the From address. Then open the headers. That is where the useful evidence lives. Open Show original In Gmail, open the message menu and click Show original . Gmail displays the raw message and a summary of its authentication checks. Start with Authentication-Results . This line tells you whether Gmail recorded dkim=pass , dkim=fail , or another result. If DKIM fails, Gmail has less reason to trust the message, which often lines up with spam placement or inconsistent inboxing across recipients. What the status means Use this table when reading Gmail headers: Gmail DKIM Authentication Results Status What It Means Your Next Step pass Gmail verified the signature against the public key in DNS If placement is still poor, check SPF, DMARC alignment, and sender reputation fail Gmail could not validate the signature Check the selector, key match, and whether a relay or forwarder changed the message neutral Gmail did not reach a strong verification result Confirm the message was signed at all and that the selector points to a valid DNS record A pass means this trust check worked. It does not mean the message will land in the inbox every time. A fail is the signal to investigate right away. In practice, I usually see one of two causes. The signer is using the wrong key or selector, or the message was modified after it was signed. What to inspect in the header Three parts usually explain the problem: Authentication-Results: Gmail's verdict DKIM-Signature: The signing domain, selector, and signing details Received lines and other routing clues: Signs that the message passed through forwarding or a third-party platform Read these together. If Authentication-Results says dkim=fail , the DKIM-Signature line tells you which domain signed the message and which selector Gmail tried to verify. That lets you connect a technical failure to the business issue. If the wrong system signed the mail, or a relay altered it, Gmail may treat your revenue email like suspicious traffic. If you want a quick DNS check before reading raw headers, use this DKIM checker for your sending domain . It helps confirm that the public key is published and readable. Then return to Gmail to see whether the live message passed verification. A simple reading sequence This is the fastest workflow for non-technical teams: Open a real delivered email in Gmail Click Show original Find Authentication-Results Look for dkim=pass , dkim=fail , or dkim=neutral If it failed, find the d= domain and s= selector in DKIM-Signature Compare that selector and domain against the DNS record you intended to publish This order matters. Start with Gmail's result on a real message, then trace back to DNS and sending tools. That is how you move from “we added the record” to “we know why Gmail did or did not trust this email.” Diagnosing Common DKIM Failures A founder sees the DNS record in place, sends a test, and still finds the message in spam with dkim=fail in Gmail. That usually means the problem is not the record itself. It means something in the sending path broke the signature after the message left the platform. The practical mistake I see is treating DKIM as a DNS task only. DNS is just one part. Gmail is checking whether the message that arrived still matches the message that was signed. If those differ, Gmail has a reason to trust the mail less, and that can push sales outreach, onboarding emails, and renewal reminders into spam. A common cause teams miss Forwarding breaks more valid DKIM setups than people expect. A message can leave your sending tool correctly signed and fail by the time it reaches Gmail because another system touched it on the way. Common examples include aliases, inbox forwarding rules, security gateways, CRM relays, and outbound tools that rewrite content or headers after signing. That is why Gmail headers matter. They show whether the failure came from the key, the selector, or a changed message. If you only check DNS, you miss the reason the live email failed. Why forwarding breaks DKIM DKIM signs specific headers and a version of the message body. Any system that changes one of those signed parts can invalidate the signature. The usual culprits are straightforward: A forwarding service adds or rewrites content , such as a footer, disclaimer, or tracking element An intermediate system changes signed headers Mail passes through multiple platforms , and one of them reprocesses the message A sales or agency workflow sends through a relay that does not preserve the original signature Partial success often misleads founders. SPF can still pass in some of these cases, so the setup looks healthy at a glance while Gmail still distrusts the message. A passing SPF result does not fix a broken DKIM signature if Gmail sees that the signed message was altered. Read the DKIM-Signature header for the actual cause The useful clues are in the header, not in the admin screenshot. Start with the d= value. That is the domain that signed the message. Then check s= , which is the selector Gmail used to find the public key in DNS. If d= points to one domain and your published key lives under another, verification fails. If s= points to an old or missing selector, verification fails. If both are correct, but Gmail still reports dkim=fail , focus on what changed in transit. For teams working through authentication as a whole, this guide to setting up DKIM, SPF, DMARC, and BIMI together helps put DKIM failures in context. A practical troubleshooting checklist When Gmail shows DKIM failure, check these in order: Signing domain Confirm that the d= domain is the one you intended to sign mail for this stream. Selector Confirm that the s= selector exists in DNS and matches the active key for that sender. Key alignment Make sure the platform that signed the message is using the private key that matches the public key published in DNS. Mail path Review whether the message went through forwarding, aliasing, a CRM relay, a help desk tool, or a secure email gateway. Message changes after signing Check for footers, rewritten links, added disclaimers, MIME changes, or header changes introduced after the original send. What usually fixes the problem The cleanest mail flow wins. Sign the message once, send it through as few systems as possible, and avoid tools that modify content after signing. If the headers show the wrong signing domain, fix the sending platform. If the selector is wrong, fix DNS or rotate the key cleanly. If forwarding changed the message, change the route or sign at the final system that sends the email. Many DKIM problems are really mail flow problems. Gmail headers let you prove that, which is what helps you fix spam placement instead of guessing. A Step-by-Step Guide to Set Up DKIM in Google Workspace Google Workspace makes DKIM setup manageable, but the process still has a few places where teams make avoidable mistakes. The cleanest approach is to generate the key in Google Admin, publish the TXT record in DNS, then return to Google to activate signing. This setup visual shows the flow clearly. Generate the DKIM key in Google Admin Inside Google Workspace Admin, go to Gmail's authentication settings and generate a new DKIM record for the sending domain. Google supports key generation in the Admin Console, and modern best practice is to use a 2048-bit key for stronger protection. The DKIM public key is then published as a DNS TXT record in a format that starts with v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p= . Add the TXT record to DNS After generation, Google provides a host name and TXT value. The record commonly uses a host name like google._domainkey.yourdomain . The DNS provider interface will vary, but the job is always the same: Copy the exact host name provided by Google Paste the full TXT value without trimming it Save the record and allow time for DNS to update To set up DKIM in Google Workspace, the required flow is to generate a key in the Admin Console, add the provided TXT record to DNS, and then start authentication. If Gmail later reports dkim=fail , Google's guidance indicates a mismatch between the private signing key and the public key in DNS. For teams that want the broader authentication stack done correctly at the same time, this guide to setting up DKIM, SPF, DMARC, and BIMI is a useful reference. Start authentication in Google Workspace Publishing the DNS record is only part of the setup. Signing doesn't begin until authentication is started inside Google Admin. That final click matters. Plenty of teams add the record and stop there. To make the flow easier to follow, this walkthrough video is useful: Verify that DKIM is actually working After activation, verification should happen in two places. Check DNS visibility Use Google Admin Toolbox or another DNS lookup method to confirm the TXT record is publicly visible. Send a test email to Gmail Open the message, click Show original, and look for DKIM pass in the header. Verification habit: Never treat "record added" as success. Success is when Gmail shows the message passing authentication. Common setup mistakes A few errors show up repeatedly: Mistake Why it happens Result Wrong selector An old or different selector was copied into DNS Gmail can't find the right public key Partial TXT value DNS interfaces can make long values awkward to paste Signature validation fails Record added, authentication not started Teams assume DNS publication turns signing on automatically Outbound mail isn't signed Old key mismatch Platform rotates or regenerates the key without DNS update Gmail shows failure The practical goal isn't just to "have DKIM." It's to have Google Workspace signing mail with the same key Gmail can retrieve from DNS. Beyond DKIM SPF, DMARC, and Sender Reputation DKIM solves one part of the problem. It proves message integrity and domain-level signing. It doesn't tell Gmail everything it wants to know. Modern deliverability depends on three authentication layers working together: SPF checks whether the sending server is authorized DKIM checks whether the message was signed and stayed intact DMARC tells receivers what policy to apply when checks fail Why all three matter If a business only sets up DKIM, Gmail still has an incomplete picture. Authentication becomes much more reliable when SPF and DMARC are aligned with it. This isn't just a compliance exercise. It's how a domain proves that its mail is legitimate across different providers, tools, and workflows. A useful broader overview of email platform decisions and sending considerations appears in the Wise Web email marketing guide , especially for teams comparing infrastructure choices. DMARC changed the baseline Gmail tightened bulk sender expectations in February 2024 by requiring a DMARC policy for bulk sending domains. The policy must be set to p=none , p=quarantine , or p=reject , and messages that fail DMARC alignment can be routed to spam or rejected. For founders, the lesson is straightforward. Authentication is now operational hygiene. It's not a side task for later. Reputation still decides what happens next Even a perfectly authenticated domain can struggle if sender reputation is weak. Mailbox providers also look at behavioral signals: Sending consistency Complaint patterns Engagement quality Bounce risk Provider-specific reputation history That's why authentication alone doesn't solve inbox placement. It removes a trust blocker. Reputation determines whether the domain is treated like a sender people want to hear from. For teams that want a deeper view of how these standards fit together, this email authentication guide covering SPF, DKIM, and DMARC is worth reading. FAQ on DKIM and Email Authentication What is DKIM in Gmail DKIM is a digital signature attached to outgoing email. Gmail uses it to verify that the message came from the claimed domain and wasn't modified after it was sent. Is DKIM required for Gmail For serious sending, yes. Gmail relies heavily on DKIM as part of its anti-spoofing and spam filtering process, and unauthenticated mail faces much more friction. What does DKIM fail mean in Gmail headers It means Gmail couldn't validate the signature against the public key published for the signing domain. That usually points to a DNS mismatch, a selector problem, or a message that changed after signing. Why does DKIM fail even when the DNS record looks correct Because DNS isn't the only variable. Forwarding services, relays, and other intermediaries can alter signed content or headers, which breaks validation even when the published key is correct. What is the difference between SPF and DKIM SPF checks whether the sending server is authorized to send for the domain. DKIM checks whether the actual message was signed by that domain and remained intact during delivery. Does Gmail need both SPF and DKIM In practice, yes. A healthier setup includes SPF, DKIM, and DMARC working together, because each covers a different part of email trust and policy enforcement. How can a team confirm DKIM is working after setup Send a test email to a Gmail account, open Show original, and read the Authentication-Results header. If Gmail shows DKIM pass, the signature validated correctly for that message. How does Mailwarm help improve sender reputation Mailwarm is a premium email warmup and deliverability platform. Does Mailwarm need access to my inbox No. Unlike basic warmup tools, Mailwarm does not require IMAP access or permission to read your private inbox. If email is part of a company's growth strategy, Mailwarm helps senders build reputation, monitor inbox placement, and reduce spam risk with expert-guided warmup. title: Toyota and 3x Latin Grammy-nominated Artist, Álvaro Díaz, Partner to Celebrate Music and Culture
summary: PLANO, TEXAS (July 30, 2026) – Toyota is partnering with 3x Latin Grammy-nominated Puerto Rican artist Álvaro Díaz to celebrate music discovery, cultural connections and fan engagement through a series of exclusive artwork inspired by his latest album, OMAKASE. The […]
body_text: Exclusive artwork inspired by Díaz’s OMAKASE album and a special Toyota Music Den performance at Lollapalooza bring fans closer to the artist’s creative journey PLANO, TEXAS (July 30, 2026) – Toyota is partnering with 3x Latin Grammy-nominated Puerto Rican artist Álvaro Díaz to celebrate music discovery, cultural connections and fan engagement through a series of exclusive artwork inspired by his latest album, OMAKASE . The collaboration brings together Toyota’s Japanese heritage and Díaz’s creative vision, which blends Japanese and Puerto Rican influences throughout the album. Conceived as a curated experience inspired by the Japanese dining tradition in which a chef guides guests through a personalized journey, OMAKASE explores the intersection of cultures, creativity and discovery. It debuted at No. 1 on Spotify’s Top Albums Debut Global chart and reached No. 1 in over 16 countries on Apple Music. To date, it has surpassed 200 million global streams. The album’s themes made Toyota a natural partner to help connect fans with Díaz’s music and artistic journey. “At Toyota, we’re passionate about helping fans discover the artists and cultural movements shaping what’s next in music,” said Paul Doleshal, general manager, motorsports and sponsorships, Toyota. “We’re thrilled to work with Álvaro Díaz, whose creativity, ambition and originality make him an exciting partner. From exclusive artwork collaborations to his upcoming performance at the Toyota Music Den during Lollapalooza, we’re proud to create experiences that bring fans closer to the artists they love while helping drive music discovery forward.” As part of the partnership, Toyota and Díaz collaborated with two distinctive artists to create a series of limited-edition posters inspired by the OMAKASE tracklist and aesthetic. Drawing from both Japanese and Puerto Rican artistic traditions, the collection features work from Shingo Yamazaki, a Japanese Korean American oil painter whose pieces explore identity, home and nostalgia, and Bikismo, the legendary Puerto Rican graffiti artist and muralist known for his vibrant, hyper-realistic metallic style. Together, the artwork celebrates the cultural fusion at the heart of the album and the partnership. Fans will have an opportunity to receive a limited-edition poster during Díaz’s special performance at the Toyota Music Den stage at Lollapalooza. The four-poster series brings the creative world of OMAKASE to life through a vibrant, street-style fusion of Latino and Japanese culture. Fans nationwide will also have opportunities to access the artwork through Toyota Latino social channels. The collaboration builds on Toyota’s commitment to supporting artists through unique music experiences that bring fans closer to the people shaping today’s music landscape. Earlier this year, Toyota introduced OMAKASE to fans during a listening experience at Sueños Music Festival, also in Chicago, and will continue the partnership through additional projects, including Sounds of the Road , presented by Toyota and SiriusXM. This exclusive performance and interview series features emerging and established artists, and Álvaro’s episode will launch later this year in Spanish. The collaboration between Toyota and established artist, Álvaro Díaz, builds on the brand’s commitment to supporting artists through unique music experiences that bring fans closer to performers shaping today’s music landscape. For more information on the partnership and videos on the creative process behind the posters, visit www.toyota.com/espanol/music/ and follow Toyota Latino on social media. title: Lanchester: The Other British Luxury Car Drafted into WWI
summary: As any student of history knows, part of the fun of flipping back through the record of how things actually happened is ruminating on how things might have happened differently. In another universe, Lee Harvey Oswald’s Carcano rifle jams. The Titanic avoids the iceberg. A British sniper sees a scrawny Austrian corporal poke his head […]
body_text: As any student of history knows, part of the fun of flipping back through the record of how things actually happened is ruminating on how things might have happened differently. In another universe, Lee Harvey Oswald’s Carcano rifle jams. The Titanic avoids the iceberg. A British sniper sees a scrawny Austrian corporal poke his head above a trench and pulls the trigger. In these alternate, imaginary timelines that flowed from those moments is different—perhaps for the better, perhaps for the worse. Open your history books to the spring of 1917 and the beginning of the Russian Revolution. Tsar Nikolai Alexandrovich Romanov has abdicated the throne, and his family is imprisoned under house arrest. In Moscow is a Royal Naval officer named Oliver Locker-Lampson, whose grandfather was captain and teacher to a young Horatio Nelson, who went on to become Britain’s greatest naval hero when he smashed Napoleon’s fleet during the Battle of the Nile in 1798. Locker-Lampson is in possession of a secret plan devised by British intelligence services to rescue the Romanovs, or at least the Tsar. Why Locker-Lampson? Though he is a lieutenant commander in the Royal Navy, as commissioned by First Lord of the Admiralty Winston Churchill, the civilian head of the navy, Locker-Lampson has a fighting force on land. His armored-car divisions and machine-gun crews stand ready to perform a daring rescue. Perhaps because of political pressure brought to bear by the royal family of the United Kingdom, the rescue never happens. A year later, in the summer of 1918, the Bolsheviks killed the Tsar and his family in a basement in Yekaterinburg. Imperial War Museum As for Locker-Lampson, he and his men spent the previous four years as a hugely mobile fighting unit in World War I (1914–1918), traveling some 53,000 miles over mountains, deserts, and arctic tundra. In sharp contrast to the stagnation of trench warfare in the war’s west theater, these armored cars have journeyed farther than any other WWI force, fighting all the way from above the Arctic Circle into the heat of Turkey and northern Persia. They engaged in action everywhere from Romania to the shadow of Mount Ararat, rumored to be the resting place of Noah’s Ark. The backbone of the Royal Navy’s British Armoured Car Expeditionary Force (ACEF) was the Lanchester armored car, a vehicle built in nearly the same quantities as the much better-known armored Rolls-Royce Ghosts . On Orders From Churchill It’s hard to picture Winston Churchill as a young man. The picture of him in most people’s heads is that famous portrait where he glowers at the camera, the epitome of bulldog determination in the face of overwhelming odds. He seems to have been born old. In 1914, Churchill was just forty, a bumptious First Lord of the Admiralty, anxious that the Royal Navy should cover itself in glory in the war ahead. Churchill, circa 1916 Public Domain Picture his meeting with the slightly younger Oliver Stillingford Locker-Lampson in some wood-paneled room, a desk in the middle that weighs as much as a Ford F-150. A Conservative Party member of a respected family, Locker-Lampson had the aforementioned connection to Horatio Nelson and was a grandson of Lord Elgin (as in The Elgin Marbles ). Locker-Lampson’s post-WWI politics are something of a rollercoaster ride. A hatred of communism from his wartime service pushed him to approve of the rise of anti-communist fascism in Italy and Germany, at least at first. This sentiment was relatively short-lived, and by 1933, he was fighting to provide refuge and citizenship to Jewish refugees fleeing Nazi persecution. One notable effort of Locker-Lampson’s was securing safety for a refugee near his home in Norfolk, England, after the man was forced to leave Belgium after receiving death threats. That man’s name was Albert Einstein. Back to Locker-Lampson and Churchill’s discreet meeting, and the understanding that was struck. Being extremely wealthy, the former had the wherewithal to pay for a fleet of armored cars out of his own personal pocket. For Churchill, that was good enough to earn an officer’s commission. The British Armoured Car Expeditionary Force (ACEF) was formed. Albert Einstein with Commander Oliver Locker-Lempson MP, 1933. Leslie Cardew/National Science and Media Museum Here’s another little historical wrinkle that’ll widen the eyes of any readers with Irish roots. Locker-Lampson was a Conservative Unionist politician, and he had connections in Ireland with the Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF), a paramilitary organization opposed to home rule in Ireland. A couple of months before WWI kicked off, the UVF had actually been successful in smuggling some 25,000 rifles into Ireland. The source was none other than Imperial Germany. Some of the money to buy these armored Lanchester cars came from UVF funds, and three of them were named after places in the north of Ireland: Londonderry, Mountjoy, and Ulster. Many of the unit’s recruits would also have been loyalist Ulstermen. As a politician and former journalist, Locker-Lampson knew that it would be no good wading into the quagmire of the Western front and spending his days sitting around or being reassigned to trench warfare. He therefore pushed to be sent to the East, where he would support the Tsar’s Russian forces. These were having a terrible time of it, and their requests for assistance spurred Churchill into one of his largest blunders, the disastrous invasion at Gallipoli in February of 1915. Imperial War Museum In the east, however, Locker-Lampson could roam free, far enough from headquarters to be his own man. In December of 1915, his division of 39 armored Lanchesters and supporting crew set sail for Russia. Embarrassingly, the radiators all froze and exploded, and the cars and men had to be shipped back home again. However, by 1916, they were back, ready to go to war. Lanchester, an Equal to Rolls-Royce At this point, it’s worth a brief look at Lanchester, a car company only a dedicated Anglophile may be aware of. The company can claim to have produced the first car fully engineered and built in Britain, in 1886. (Lanchester is still technically in existence as a subsidiary of Tata, although nothing is actually built under the name.) This pioneering spirit set Lanchester up for further advances, including the development of the very first disc-type brakes in 1902. By 1913, the company offered a fairly conventional luxury touring car, fitted with a 5.5-liter inline-six good for just under 40 hp. (The Ford Model T, for context, had 22 hp.) This output made the Lanchester very competitive with the contemporary Silver Ghost from Rolls-Royce, and Lanchester’s build quality was praised at the time. Imperial War Museum In armored form, both the Ghost and the Lanchester look very similar, as the turret was standardized between the two cars. It’s up front that the difference is noticeable, with the Lanchester having sloping front armor. This makes it look very much like Roberto, the knife-wielding robot from Futurama . The Lanchester was certainly a pretty dangerous and alarming foe if you were an enemy combatant with nothing more than a bolt-action rifle. Imperial War Museum Thanks to a top speed of as much as 50 mph, the Lanchester armored cars were fearsome strike weapons. When supporting infantry, they were essentially rolling bunkers. However, they weren’t particularly effective in helping Russian forces repel attacks from troops allied with the Imperial German forces, because Russian morale had begun to fray badly. Still, the sight of a Lanchester roaring into battle, its Vickers .303 belching flame and lead, Cossack cavalry riding close behind, was certainly impressive. The tales of the squadron’s exploits were maximized by Locker-Lampson, who could spin a good yarn, and they provided a welcome distraction from the meat-grinder tales from the Western front. It helped when Germany’s Kaiser put a reported bounty of 20,000 Marks on Locker-Lampson’s head. Imperial War Museum Eventually, the Russian Revolution put an end to things. Despite negotiations with the new administration that provided resupply, the squadron often found itself covering the retreat of demoralized Russian troops. Only a third of the Lanchesters survived. As a final insult, revolutionary Russian forces eventually confiscated the last of the cars and equipment, and the British went back to England without their material. Locker-Lampson never forgave the betrayal. Imperial War Museum Imperial War Museum Imperial War Museum Many of the men Locker-Lampson had led were snapped up by other armored regiments, eager to make the most of their experience. Many ended up in the amusingly named Dunsterforce, a small and secretive team in contemporary Persia that trained local irregular troops and fought the Ottoman Empire, much as Lawrence of Arabia had done. Locker-Lampson ended his career in politics in 1945, having spent the 1930s as one of the few supporters of Churchill. He was active in opposing appeasement of German and Italian aggression leading up to the war, and actively campaigned against British fascists like Walter Mosley and managed to get raging antisemite Arnold Leese locked up in 1936. Imperial War Museum Reliable, fast, and in some aspects a better fighting platform than the Rolls-Royce, the armored Lanchester found itself part of a story that was popular with audiences at the time, but has long since faded. A second generation of the vehicles was built after WWI, but proved too bulky to be effective. Lanchester faded with the Great Depression. Time has not entirely forgotten the tale of Locker-Lampson and his adventuring Lanchesters, but they are nowhere near as well-known as the exploits of the armored Rolls-Royce Ghosts. Perhaps, had history taken a different turn that saw him actually rescue the Romanovs, the names of both would be better known. title: Wedding Ceremony Music Guide: Songs for Every Moment (2026)
summary: A wedding ceremony needs music for 5 distinct moments: the prelude (guests arrive), the processional (wedding party entrance), the bride's processional,
body_text: Last Updated on July 20, 2026 by Joy Editors A wedding ceremony needs music for 5 distinct moments: the prelude (guests arrive), the processional (wedding party entrance), the bride’s processional, any musical interludes during the ceremony, and the recessional (couple exits). Plan for 6 to 10 songs total. Choose songs below 80 BPM for the processional — slow enough for a composed walk down the aisle. Wedding ceremony music does more than fill silence. It sets the emotional tone before a single word is spoken, signals transitions between moments, and creates the soundtrack guests will associate with your wedding for years. Getting it right requires more planning than most couples expect. This guide walks through every music moment in a wedding ceremony, what to look for in each, specific song recommendations, and how to work with musicians or a DJ to make it seamless. The 5 Music Moments in a Wedding Ceremony Most ceremonies have five distinct music moments. Understanding each one helps you plan the right songs for the right purpose. 1. Prelude (Guests Arriving) The prelude plays as guests arrive and find their seats, typically 20 to 30 minutes before the ceremony begins. It sets the mood and signals to guests that the event is starting. Choose 6 to 10 songs that reflect your overall aesthetic — classical, acoustic, jazz, or contemporary. The prelude should feel welcoming and unhurried. Avoid songs that are too emotionally charged for background listening. This is ambient music, not a performance moment. 2. Wedding Party Processional The processional plays as the wedding party walks down the aisle — bridesmaids, groomsmen, flower girls, and ring bearers. This is typically a single song, though longer wedding parties sometimes use two. The tempo should be slow enough for a composed walk: aim for 60 to 80 BPM. Many couples choose a different song for the wedding party processional than for the bride’s entrance, creating a clear distinction between the two moments. 3. Bride’s Processional (The Entrance) The most emotionally significant music moment in the ceremony. This is the song playing as the bride walks down the aisle. It should feel personal and meaningful — not just popular. The tempo needs to match the pace of the walk and the length of the aisle. Classic choices like Pachelbel’s “Canon in D” or Wagner’s “Bridal Chorus” remain timeless, but contemporary options such as “A Thousand Years” by Christina Perri and “Turning Page” by Sleeping at Last are increasingly popular. 4. Ceremony Interludes (Optional) Some ceremonies include musical moments between readings, during a unity ceremony (candle lighting, sand ceremony, handfasting), or as a standalone performance. These are entirely optional — many ceremonies have no music during the vows and readings, and that is perfectly fine. If you choose an interlude, keep it to one or two songs maximum. More than that stretches the ceremony and dilutes the emotional impact. 5. Recessional The recessional plays as the newly married couple walks back down the aisle, followed by the wedding party. This is the most upbeat music moment — it is a celebration. The energy should shift noticeably from the ceremony’s solemnity to joy and excitement. Songs like “Signed, Sealed, Delivered” by Stevie Wonder and “Best Day of My Life” by American Authors are popular choices, but anything that makes you smile works here. Song Recommendations by Ceremony Moment Prelude Songs “Clair de Lune” — Debussy (timeless, elegant) “The Book of Love” — Peter Gabriel (warm, understated) “La Vie en Rose” — Louis Armstrong (romantic, classic) “Bloom” — The Paper Kites (modern indie, gentle) “Songbird” — Fleetwood Mac (familiar, emotional without being dramatic) “River Flows in You” — Yiruma (popular piano piece, ambient) Wedding Party Processional Songs “Canon in D” — Pachelbel (the quintessential choice) “Marry Me” — Train (sweet, recognizable) “Here Comes the Sun” — The Beatles (cheerful, optimistic) “Latch (Acoustic)” — Sam Smith (modern, emotional) “Flightless Bird, American Mouth” — Iron & Wine (intimate, cinematic) Bride’s Processional Songs (The Entrance) “A Thousand Years” — Christina Perri (the most popular modern choice) “Bridal Chorus” — Wagner (traditional, instantly recognizable) “Turning Page” — Sleeping at Last (cinematic, emotional) “Can’t Help Falling in Love” — Elvis Presley (timeless, universally loved) “Ave Maria” — Schubert (classical, sacred) “At Last” — Etta James (jazz standard, deeply emotional) Recessional Songs “Signed, Sealed, Delivered (I’m Yours)” — Stevie Wonder “Best Day of My Life” — American Authors “You Make My Dreams” — Hall & Oates “Happy” — Pharrell Williams “Beautiful Day” — U2 “I Gotta Feeling” — Black Eyed Peas How Many Songs Do You Need for a Wedding Ceremony? Moment Number of Songs Duration Prelude 6–10 songs 20–30 minutes Wedding party processional 1–2 songs 2–5 minutes Bride’s processional 1 song 1–2 minutes Interludes 0–2 songs 0–6 minutes Recessional 1 song 2–3 minutes For a standard 30-minute ceremony, plan for 6 to 10 songs total across all moments. Longer ceremonies (Catholic mass, Hindu ceremony) may need additional prelude and interlude music. Live Music vs. Recorded Music for the Ceremony Option Best For Limitations Cost Range String quartet Classic elegance, church settings Limited repertoire for modern songs $800–$2,500 Solo musician (guitar, piano, harp) Intimate, personal, more affordable Single instrument range $300–$800 DJ / sound system Any song available, consistent volume, flexible Less personal, requires setup $500–$1,500 Spotify / playlist Free or very low cost, complete control Requires reliable sound system, no live feel $0–$200 (equipment rental) Vocalist with accompanist Emotional impact, memorable Expensive, requires rehearsal $500–$1,500 Pro tip: If your venue has poor acoustics or is outdoors, a DJ with a quality sound system often delivers more consistent results than live musicians who may struggle with wind, echo, or distance. Ask your venue coordinator what they recommend. Working with Your Ceremony Musician or DJ Clear communication with your music provider prevents the most common ceremony music mistakes. What to tell your musician or DJ The exact songs you want for each moment, with backup options When to start and stop each song (full song, fade out, or specific cue) The cue for the bride’s entrance (who signals them, and how) Whether you want instrumental versions, original recordings, or live performance Any songs you absolutely do not want played Timing the processional Walk the aisle before the wedding day to understand the timing. Count your steps, note the length, and communicate this to your musician. A 50-foot aisle at a comfortable pace takes approximately 45 to 60 seconds. A 100-foot cathedral aisle can take 90 seconds or more. For the bride’s processional, many musicians recommend starting the song 8 to 10 seconds before the bride begins walking, so the music is established before she appears. Coordinate this cue clearly with whoever is signaling the musician. Keep everyone on schedule Once you have finalized your ceremony timeline, add it to your Joy wedding website and enable the Event Countdown. Guests will always know how many days remain until the celebration, while your website keeps ceremony times, locations, and other important details up to date in one place. For a full walkthrough on managing schedules across multiple events, see this guide . Religious and Cultural Ceremony Music Considerations Catholic churches: Many require pre-approval of all music. Sacred music is often required for the ceremony itself. Popular secular songs may be restricted to the prelude and recessional, or not permitted at all. Jewish ceremonies: Traditional ceremonies often include the Hava Nagila for the recessional. Reform ceremonies are typically more flexible. Hindu ceremonies: Music varies significantly by regional tradition. Consult with the pandit early about what is appropriate. Outdoor venues: Check local noise ordinances and whether amplification is permitted. Keep Your Wedding Weekend Organized Your ceremony is only one part of the celebration. If you are also hosting a rehearsal dinner, welcome party, after-party, or farewell brunch, create each as a separate event on your Joy wedding website . Guests can view a complete itinerary for the weekend, while Private Events ensure each guest only sees the events they are invited to. This creates a personalized schedule without requiring separate websites or invitations. This approach is especially helpful for destination weddings , where guests need clear logistics for multi-day celebrations across unfamiliar locations. Wedding Ceremony Music Checklist Confirm venue music policy (restrictions, amplification rules) Book musician or DJ 6 to 12 months in advance Choose prelude songs (6–10 tracks) Choose wedding party processional song Choose bride’s processional song Choose recessional song Decide on any ceremony interludes Walk the aisle to time the processional Brief musician/DJ on all cues and transitions Confirm sound system setup and backup plan Share final song list with officiant Add your ceremony to your Joy wedding website schedule Enable the Event Countdown so guests can easily track how close the wedding day is If hosting additional celebrations, create separate schedule items and use Private Events so guests only see the events they are invited to Frequently Asked Questions What songs do you need for a wedding ceremony? At minimum: a prelude playlist (6–10 songs), a processional song for the wedding party, a processional song for the bride, and a recessional. Optional: interludes during readings or unity ceremonies. Plan for 6 to 10 songs total for a standard 30-minute ceremony. What tempo should the processional song be? Aim for 60 to 80 BPM for the processional. This is slow enough for a composed, unhurried walk down the aisle. Songs above 90 BPM tend to feel rushed. Test the tempo by walking to the song before the wedding day. Can you use popular songs at a wedding ceremony? Yes, in most cases. If your ceremony is in a religious venue, check with the officiant first — some churches restrict secular music during the ceremony itself. For civil ceremonies and most outdoor venues, any song is permitted. How far in advance should you book a wedding musician? Book 6 to 12 months in advance for popular dates (May through October). Quality musicians book quickly for peak wedding season. If you are planning a last-minute wedding, ask about availability directly — cancellations do happen. Do you need music during the ceremony itself, or just for the processional and recessional? You do not need music during the ceremony itself. Many couples have no music during the vows, readings, and ring exchange. Others add a single live performance during a unity ceremony or reading. The processional, any interludes, and the recessional are the three essential music moments. What is the most popular wedding processional song? “A Thousand Years” by Christina Perri and “Canon in D” by Pachelbel consistently rank as the most popular processional songs. “Marry Me” by Train and “All of Me” by John Legend are also widely chosen. The most important factor is choosing a song that feels meaningful to you, not just popular.
